title: a11y screenshot: focusless capture, multi-node, cross-root, subprocess
desc: wkappbot a11y screenshot is fully focusless -- never steals keyboard focus or changes z-order. Supports multi-node composite, cross-root windows, UIA scope crop, MDI form mode, subprocess usage. Use this instead of any manual PrintWindow/mss/click approach.
steps: BASIC USAGE: wkappbot a11y screenshot GRAP [-o output.png]. Focusless -- NO click, NO SetForegroundWindow, NO z-order change. Just pass the window grap. Output last stdout line: SAVED:PATH. Example: wkappbot a11y screenshot nfrunlite -o snap.png

FOCUSLESS GUARANTEE: screenshot NEVER steals keyboard focus or changes window z-order. Safe during live trading, real-time feeds, any latency-sensitive context. If your code calls SetForegroundWindow or a11y click before capturing -- REMOVE IT. wkappbot handles occlusion internally via PrintWindow PW_RENDERFULLCONTENT.

MULTI-NODE MODE: pass 2+ grap args OR single grap with UIA #scope. Captures each target independently, composites to union bounding box, masks pixels outside any target rect to alpha=0. Cross-root windows work. Example: wkappbot a11y screenshot TAB_GRAP GRID_GRAP -o combined.png
SINGLE vs MULTI: Single grap no scope -> full-window capture (fastest). Single grap + #scope (UIA element) -> crops to that element. Two or more graps -> union composite of all targets.
FORM MODE for MDI apps: wkappbot a11y screenshot GRAP --form FORM_ID -- captures a specific MDI child form e.g. nfrunlite [2000] holdings panel.

OCCLUSION HANDLING: PrintWindow PW_RENDERFULLCONTENT renders the window even when partially or fully occluded -- no need to bring it to front. GPU/DirectX windows fall back to screen-coordinate capture.

SUBPROCESS USAGE (Python): use subprocess.run with args WKBOT a11y screenshot GRAP --out path, capture_output True, timeout 15 seconds; success is returncode equal 0. NEVER add SetForegroundWindow or click before this.
SEE ALSO: a11y-screenshot-usage-ref for dated LIVE CASE fix history (GDI+ capture retry, OCR image-load retry, the major OCR Vision-restore fix).
